Index of the documentation for recipe-book, the Nag Family Recipes site.

Updated 2026-10-24 · Source README.md

recipe-book documentation

recipe-book is Nag Family Recipes, a NYT Cooking–style recipe site for the family at recipes.nag.family. It turns a YouTube playlist and an Apple Notes folder into static recipe pages, with search and category filtering, and needs no login, database or runtime configuration.

Status: built and in production on Cloudflare Workers since 2026-10-21.

Terms used throughout

Term Meaning
Recipe One .mdx file under content/recipes/; all its data is YAML front matter
Slug A recipe's URL name, /recipe/<slug>; unique across every source folder
Source Where a recipe came from: youtube, notes or manual, and the folder it lives in
Rewrite The pass by scripts/rewrite_recipes.py in which Claude cleans a new recipe's title, ingredients and steps
Worker The Cloudflare Worker recipe-book that serves the site, built with OpenNext

For Use

stableeveryone

What the recipe site is, how it is put together, and what is in and out of scope.

Updated 2026-10-24 · Source 01-overview.md · Read first: recipe-book documentation

Overview

What it is

A public recipe site for the Nag family. The recipes come from two places the family already uses: a YouTube playlist of cooking videos and a "Recipes" folder in Apple Notes. Each one becomes a page with ingredients, steps, times and, for videos, the embedded video.

How it is put together

YouTube playlist ──ingest_youtube.py──┐
                                      ├─▶ content/recipes/<source>/*.mdx ──rewrite_recipes.py──▶ cleaned .mdx
Apple Notes "Recipes" ─ingest_notes.py┘                                                              │
                                                                                                     ▼
                                   next build: src/lib/recipes.ts reads every .mdx with fs ──▶ static pages
                                                                                                     │
                                                                          OpenNext ──▶ Worker recipe-book
Part Where
Framework Next.js 16 App Router, Tailwind 4, npm
Pages /, /recipe/[slug], /category/[category], all prerendered with generateStaticParams
Data src/lib/recipes.ts, reading content/recipes/ at build time
Search Fuse.js in the browser (src/components/SearchBar.tsx)
Images public/images/recipes/
Structured data JSON-LD on each recipe page
Hosting Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext; see 03 Deploy

Scope

In scope: reading recipes, searching them, filtering by category, and adding recipes through the two syncs or by hand.

Out of scope: accounts, comments, editing in the browser, a database, and any runtime environment variable. Every change to a recipe is a commit and a rebuild.

What stays hard

  • Every push to main deploys, including the sync bots' commits, so a bad recipe file reaches production unless the build fails on it.
  • Slugs are one namespace across all sources. Two recipes with the same title from different sources clash; see Slugs.

stabledevelopers

The recipe file format, the three sources and their syncs, the slug rule, and the Claude rewrite.

Updated 2026-10-24 · Source 02-recipes.md · Read first: recipe-book documentation, Overview

Recipes

The file

A recipe is an .mdx file in content/recipes/youtube/, content/recipes/notes/ or content/recipes/manual/. Everything is front matter; the body is unused. The fields are the Recipe type in src/lib/types.ts.

Field Required Meaning
title yes Display title
slug no URL name; defaults to the file name without .mdx
description yes One or two sentences under the title
source yes youtube, notes or manual
category yes List; each value becomes a /category/<value> page
ingredients yes List of strings
instructions yes List of strings, one per step
dateAdded yes YYYY-MM-DD; the home page sorts by it, newest first
tags no List; searched by Fuse.js
cuisine, prepTime, cookTime, totalTime, servings no Shown on the page as given
sourceUrl, youtubeVideoId, image, author, datePublished no Set by the YouTube sync
notes no Free text shown after the steps
rewritten no true once the rewrite has run; the rewrite skips it then

The sources

Source How a recipe arrives Runs
youtube make sync-youtube (scripts/ingest_youtube.py): one file per playlist video, parsed from its description, thumbnail saved Weekly in .github/workflows/sync-recipes.yml, Monday 06:00 UTC, which also rewrites and commits to main
notes make sync-notes: scripts/export_notes.applescript exports the Apple Notes "Recipes" folder, scripts/ingest_notes.py writes the files By hand, or scripts/sync-notes.sh under launchd, which also rewrites, commits and pushes
manual A file written by hand in content/recipes/manual/ By hand

The YouTube sync knows a video by its youtubeVideoId, so renaming a YouTube file is safe. It also deletes the file of any video that has left the playlist. The Notes sync knows a note by the file notes/<slugified title>.mdx, so renaming a Notes file makes the next sync add it again.

Repo secrets for the weekly sync: YOUTUBE_PLAYLIST_URL, YOUTUBE_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

Slugs

A slug is unique across all three folders, because pages are routed by slug alone. Two guards keep it that way:

  • scripts/rewrite_recipes.py checks every folder before it takes a slug. On a clash it appends the slugified author (or the source), then -2, -3… as needed.
  • getAllRecipes in src/lib/recipes.ts throws on a duplicate slug, naming both files, so the build and the deploy fail instead of one page silently shadowing the other.

generateStaticParams returns raw slugs. Route params can arrive percent-encoded (slugs may hold Devanagari, categories may hold spaces), so pages decode them with decodeParam.

The rewrite

make rewrite (scripts/rewrite_recipes.py) sends each recipe without rewritten: true to Claude (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Claude returns a clean title, description, category, cuisine, times, servings, ingredients, steps, notes and tags. The script keeps the source fields (source, sourceUrl, youtubeVideoId, image, author, dateAdded, datePublished), sets rewritten: true, and renames the file when the new title gives a new slug.

stabledevelopers

How the site is hosted on Cloudflare Workers, how a push deploys it, and how to check a deploy.

Updated 2026-10-24 · Source 03-deploy.md · Read first: recipe-book documentation, Overview

Deploy

Where it runs

The Worker recipe-book, built with OpenNext (@opennextjs/cloudflare), serves recipes.nag.family as a custom domain and https://recipe-book.narendranag-cd1.workers.dev. Vercel hosted the site until 2026-10-21; that project is deleted, so there is no fallback.

File What it sets
wrangler.jsonc The Worker, its assets, and the custom domain (routes, custom_domain: true); no secrets
open-next.config.ts The static-assets incremental cache: read-only, so no ISR
public/_headers /_next/static/* immutable

Pages read fs at build time and would fail if rendered per request, which is why the cache is the static-assets one. A new recipe needs a rebuild.

How a change reaches production

.github/workflows/deploy.yml runs npm run deploy on every push to main, using the repo secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID. The sync bots push to main too (see The sources), so their recipes deploy without review. Work that isn't ready goes on a branch.

Commands

The justfile wraps these: just setup (npm ci), just test (the build), just lint (tsc --noEmit, ESLint, docs-build --check docs), just run, just build, just preview, just deploy.

Command Does
npm run dev Next dev server at http://localhost:3000
npm run build Next build; fails on a duplicate slug
npm run lint ESLint
npm run preview OpenNext build run under workerd, the local Worker test
npm run deploy OpenNext build and deploy to Workers

Test the Worker with npm run preview, not wrangler dev after a build: prerendered pages only reach .open-next/assets in OpenNext's populate-cache step, which preview and deploy run.

npm 11 gates install scripts. allowScripts in package.json pins esbuild and workerd by version, so after bumping either run npm install-scripts approve esbuild workerd.

Checking a deploy

Request every route key in .next/prerender-manifest.json and expect 200. Keys can hold non-ASCII characters, so encode each once with encodeURI(decodeURI(key)). A badly formed URL such as /recipe/%E0%A4 returns 500 from Next's router before page code runs; that is expected.

The custom domain attach is refused (code 100117) while a DNS record Cloudflare doesn't manage exists for the hostname, and override_existing_dns_record doesn't change that.
